title: Reducing and adapting to climate change

draft.title: Reducing and adapting to climate change
card: actions that cut greenhouse gas emissions, so that less warming happens. Examples are using solar and wind power instead of burning coal, and planting trees.
actions that prepare for changes already happening or expected. Examples are building sea walls and growing heat-tolerant crops.
Mitigation tackles the cause of the problem. Adaptation deals with the effects.
Communities, businesses and governments can use both at the same time.
draft.remember: Mitigation cuts emissions. Adaptation prepares for the effects.

a.q: A town replaces its coal-fired power station with a wind farm. What is this an example of?
opts: Mitigation, because it cuts greenhouse gas emissions
Adaptation, because it prepares for a warmer climate
Adaptation, because it uses a new technology
Mitigation, because it protects the town from floods
a.why: Wind power produces far fewer greenhouse gases than burning coal, so it cuts emissions and is mitigation. It does not prepare the town for changes, so it is not adaptation.
a.clue: Does it cut emissions or prepare for effects?

b.q: A farming group in Western Australia switches to wheat varieties that cope with hotter, drier seasons. What is this?
opts: Adaptation, because it prepares for changed conditions
Mitigation, because it lowers the farm's emissions
Mitigation, because it makes the climate cooler
Adaptation, because it stops greenhouse gases rising
b.why: The new wheat helps farmers cope with heat and dry seasons, so it is adaptation. It does not cut emissions or cool the climate, which is what mitigation aims to do.
b.clue: Is the change helping farmers cope or cutting emissions?

a.best: Mitigation, because it cuts greenhouse gas emissions

b.best: Adaptation, because it prepares for changed conditions

problems.detail: Mitigation is defined only as actions that 'cut greenhouse gas emissions', but planting trees is given as an example. Trees remove CO2 from the air rather than cutting emissions, so the example clashes with the definition. The definition should also cover removing greenhouse gases, or the example should be changed.

Why (b) says cooling the climate is 'what mitigation aims to do'. The card says mitigation means less warming happens. It aims to limit warming, not to make the climate cooler, so this could mislead students about what mitigation achieves.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. However, the card defines mitigation as cutting emissions yet gives tree planting, which removes CO2, as an example. Why (b) also wrongly says mitigation aims to cool the climate rather than limit warming.
